c.tagline: North Sulawesi's seafront capital — gateway to Bunaken's world-class reefs and fiery Minahasa cooking.

taxi.fareNote: Metered blue taxis exist, but many trips are agreed as a flat fare before you set off; Grab and Gojek give upfront in-app pricing and are usually the easiest option.

emergency.note: 112 is the general emergency line that reaches police, ambulance and fire; English is limited, so ask hotel or dive-resort staff to help relay.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in crowded markets like Pasar 45 and keep valuables out of sight at night.

hood_desc: The historic downtown around Pasar 45 and the old harbor, with the city's oldest churches, Ban Hin Kiong temple, the Kampung Arab quarter and the busiest markets; the central, if congested, base for exploring old Manado on foot.

The reclaimed waterfront strip along Piere Tendean Boulevard, home to the Megamas and Manado Town Square malls, seafront cafes, bars and the city's main nightlife and dining scene; the liveliest area for evenings out.
A largely residential and commercial district inland from the coast, with quieter streets, local eateries and mid-range hotels; a calmer, everyday-Manado base a short ride from the boulevard.

The southern coastal district where the boulevard tapers into a string of seafront seafood warungs famous for grilled fish and sunset views; a relaxed, resort-leaning stretch popular for its beaches and dive access.

The island neighborhood within Bunaken National Park, reached by boat from the mainland; a cluster of dive and snorkel resorts on white-sand shores at the edge of some of the world's richest coral walls.
lodging: Mercure Manado Tateli Resort and Convention

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only, as throughout Indonesia.

transit.hours: Mikrolets run roughly 5:00 AM to 8:00 PM with no fixed timetable, simply departing when reasonably full; after dark, Grab, Gojek and taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Manado has no rail or metro; the backbone of public transport is the mikrolet (angkot) share-taxi network of color-coded minibuses, supplemented by DAMRI buses and by Grab and Gojek app rides.
transit.pay: Mikrolet and bus fares are paid in cash to the driver (a few thousand rupiah per ride); there is no smartcard system, while Grab and Gojek are paid in-app or in cash.

ferry: Boats to Bunaken and Siladen islands
Pelni ships and passenger boats to other Indonesian ports

transit.m: DAMRI airport bus to the city center (~45 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary; rounding up the bill, tipping dive guides and boat crews, or leaving small change for good service is welcomed but not expected.
